prompts.prompt:
Generate ONE new narrative film frame continuing the original 1987 New York detective story Last Bus Testimony, wide approximately 2.33:1 composition with no black bars.
Reference roles: image 1 (the user's dusk street) controls environment/person scale, layered observation through real glass and muted broad daylight color. Its specific people, parked police car, pose, shop names, reflection figure and exact street must not be copied. Image 2 (the user's apartment) contributes only soft grain-bearing old-film-print response, selective detail and a dark physical viewing foreground; do not bring its room or lamp into the street. Image 3 is the current bus story master, controlling these two original men, their outfits and grounded dramatic language. Images 4 and 5 are identity and wardrobe references only; absolutely no gray studio backdrop, neutral studio light, standing model pose or split-panel layout may transfer. The new scene and actual light sources determine the final picture, preserving the user's subdued old-film-frame style.

A deliberate time ellipsis: first dawn some time after the bus conversation, on a wet ordinary 1987 New York avenue beside the precinct. Both detectives have just left the bus and are walking toward a recessed municipal brick doorway on the opposite part of the sidewalk, three-quarter side/back view. This is a new exterior design, not an exact location reconstruction from the user's street photograph. The older lean receding-haired moustached man in his brown-gray herringbone overcoat and brown suit is a half-step ahead. He has closed the palm-size cassette case and placed it in his INNER overcoat pocket; his right hand is finishing withdrawing from the pocket as his left hand releases the lapel. Do not show a loose second cassette or an open box. The younger Black clean-shaven short-haired man in deep navy overcoat, charcoal suit, light blue shirt and muted burgundy tie walks beside him, still carrying ONE plain white coffee cup low in his RIGHT hand. He glances toward his older partner. Their silence and guarded proximity carry the return to a compromised workplace, no heroic stride.

The camera remains INSIDE the stopped bus and watches them through a side window from a real empty seat. A dark near seat/back and window frame occupy a substantial side/lower foreground, with subtle old glass reflection that does not erase the action. The men belong in the middle distance and occupy a modest portion of the wide image, leaving the brick entrance, pavement and awakening street to carry visual weight. They are not two frontal fashion figures filling the frame. Keep enough silhouette, profile and garment information to recognize continuity without lighting their faces for identification.

Cool gray-blue first daylight fills street-level shadows; pale warm light reaches the upper brickwork and a few old amber streetlights remain on. Keep their colors distinct and restrained. Low midtones and dense bus-interior foreground, soft pale highlight transitions, matte damp wool, ordinary wet sidewalk with broad subdued reflections. The tiny men do not display every pore or herringbone fiber. Natural, slightly softened old print detail and fine irregular grain as in images 1–2, no HDR, digital sharpening, glossy neon, excessive orange reflections, fog or distress overlay. Period background may include one distant boxy ordinary sedan and shuttered stores without legible new text; avoid contemporary vehicles and screens. Single image, no poster, captions or watermark.

prompts.prompt:
Create ONE photographic narrative frame for the SAME original 1987 New York crime drama Last Bus Testimony, approximately 2.33:1 wide composition, no black bars, captions, title or watermark. This is a closer scene view inside the continuing drama, not a studio portrait or an evidence display.
The user's preferred image response has priority over asset-sheet presentation: dense dark foreground and low midtones, patchy practical illumination, soft pale highlights, subdued olive-gray/earth colors, matte cloth and ordinary skin, slightly softened old-film-print edges and integrated fine irregular grain. No independent face fill, glamour light, digitally etched coat fibers, pore emphasis, HDR shadow lifting or glittering wet glass. The closer camera may reveal a little more detail naturally, but must not become a clean contemporary actor headshot. Reference-sheet gray backgrounds, split panels, standing poses and neutral work light must never transfer.
Input roles: image 1 = current master with authoritative story/look; image 2 = the user's office visual grammar only, no source faces/props; image 3 = older man identity/wardrobe only; image 4 = cassette/case object only, never its tabletop or studio illumination; image 5 = current empty bus's visible construction and source light.

The next beat after image 1, a few seconds later. The older detective is still in the same window-side seat at frame left, opposite his younger partner across the aisle. Camera moves to a plausible seated position just beside/behind the younger partner's shoulder on the other side of the aisle. Medium-close three-quarter view of the older man, including his upper torso and both hands low in frame. Keep actual bus window/paneling behind him and a subdued navy shoulder/seat edge along the right/lower foreground, so the camera observes a relationship inside a space. His face must not fill the whole wide composition.

His LEFT hand supports one small clear cassette case at lap/waist level. His RIGHT fingers gently bring its lid toward the base, paused HALF CLOSED at roughly 50 degrees. The black cassette remains inside. Preserve the plain white insert with its thin red diagonal slash and tiny broken paper-seal remnants on the same physical outer short edge as image 4 when visible; do not turn the case into a large recorder or mirror its construction. The object is not lifted toward the audience. He has just raised his eyes from the case toward his partner, looking off-camera to FRAME RIGHT while his chin stays slightly lowered. A small guarded look and arrested hand movement, not theatrical surprise. The half-closed lid and change of gaze are the current story action; no fully closed/open state simultaneously and no duplicates.

Keep the lean receding-haired, small-moustached man and his exact brown-gray herringbone overcoat, brown suit/waistcoat, off-white shirt and dark brown tie. The herringbone is subdued under low practical light, not crisply engraved. The existing fluorescent fixture farther along the bus finds only part of his cheek, shirt edge and hands; coat recesses and the nearer partner's shoulder remain dark. Weak amber window spill is quiet and desaturated. His face is readable without beauty fill or symmetrical bright eyes. No neutral gray backdrop, new passengers, desk, telephone, gun, added rim light, fog or new light sources.
